title: A tally counter for the door
prompt:
Ms. Gridlock wants to count customers at the front door and the back door. The blueprint, `Counter`, is half built. Its `__init__` already gives each new counter a `count` of 0.

Fill in the two methods. `click` adds one to *this* counter. `reset` puts *this* counter back to zero. Two counters must never share a count.

When it works, the program prints `Customers so far: 2`.
hints: Inside a method, `self` is the counter you called it on. Its count lives in `self.count`.
To add one, read the old count, add 1, and store it back on `self`.
explain_after:
Calling `Counter()` ran `__init__` [py-126], so each counter got its own `count`. When you wrote `door.click()`, Python passed `door` in as the first argument, the one named `self` [py-127]. That is how `click` knew which counter to change.

`count` is an instance variable, so it belongs to one counter only [py-128]. That is why the front door and the back door keep separate tallies.
